splice.name: commit
splice.desc: Commit the staged changes (\n for a new line); --file: the message from a file, alone: written to one for your editor

splice.name: amend
splice.desc: Amend the last commit (keeps its message if none given); --file alone: its message in a file for your editor

splice.name: fixup
splice.desc: Make the staged changes a fix for an earlier commit (picked from a list), then fold it in

splice.name: absorb
splice.desc: Each staged hunk becomes a fixup! for the branch's commit that last changed its lines (shows where, asks), then folds them in

splice.name: checkout
splice.desc: Switch to a branch, tag or commit

splice.name: branch
splice.desc: Create a branch and switch to it

splice.name: delete
splice.desc: Delete a branch (local or remote) or a tag

splice.name: cleanup
splice.desc: Delete branches and remove worktrees with nothing of yours on them, and merged PRs' branches on the remote (asks first)

splice.name: cleanup-keep
splice.desc: Keep a branch (or a pattern of them, * for anything) on the remote when /cleanup runs; alone, the list

splice.name: doctor
splice.desc: A health check of the repository: what looks wrong, what to do about it, and doing what Splice can (asks first)

splice.name: merge
splice.desc: Merge a ref into the current branch

splice.name: cherry-pick
splice.desc: Copy a commit onto the current branch, or the commits in a..b, oldest first (asks first)

splice.name: range-diff
splice.desc: What the branch's last rebase, amend or reset changed in each commit (the current branch if none given); or compare two versions

splice.name: rebase
splice.desc: Rebase the current branch onto a ref (-i: edit the commits after it)

splice.name: forecast
splice.desc: Whether merging a branch with the default branch (or base) would conflict, and in which files (git merge-tree)

splice.name: compare
splice.desc: Full diff of what a branch adds to the default branch (or to base)

splice.name: fetch
splice.desc: Fetch all remotes and prune deleted branches

splice.name: sync
splice.desc: Fetch, then fast-forward every local branch that is only behind its upstream; says which have diverged or lost theirs

splice.name: update-branch
splice.desc: Rebase the current branch onto the latest default branch (or base); --stack moves the branches stacked with it too

splice.name: pull
splice.desc: Pull the current branch

splice.name: push
splice.desc: Push the current branch (sets the upstream the first time; asks first if its commits have big files or secrets); to another remote if named

splice.name: verify
splice.desc: Each commit's signature (good, bad, unknown, none, expired) in the commits a push would send, or in a range; lists the unsigned and bad ones first

splice.name: secrets
splice.desc: Secrets in the history: keys, tokens and passwords the commits added (the current branch, all, or a range), whether each is still in the working tree, and how to rotate and purge it

splice.name: risk
splice.desc: How risky the commits a push would send look (churn, whose files, size, tests), and why

splice.name: checks
splice.desc: The checks run before a push (package.json's test and lint, dotnet test, Hail's .http files, or .splice/checks.json): a list (↵ runs one); on or off here, run them now, edit writes the file

splice.name: remote
splice.desc: The remotes: list them, or add <name> <url>, rename <old> <new>, remove <name>, set-url <name> <url>

splice.name: upstream
splice.desc: Set the branch a local branch tracks (--unset to stop)

splice.name: stash
splice.desc: Stash all changes (untracked files too, unless set off in /settings), with an optional message

splice.name: sparse
splice.desc: Sparse checkout: alone, whether it is on (cone mode or not) and its folders; set <folder…> checks out only those (asks first), add brings more back (alone: pick one), off everything

splice.name: submodules
splice.desc: Every submodule: the commit recorded against the one it has, its branch and its own changes; open, update, fetch or sync one

splice.name: submodule-update
splice.desc: Initialise and check out the recorded commit of every submodule, or one

splice.name: lfs
splice.desc: Git LFS: alone, its files (downloaded or only pointers) and git lfs status; pull or fetch the files; the locks, or lock or unlock a file

splice.name: ignore
splice.desc: Add a pattern to the repository's .gitignore (i on a file in Changes offers some)

splice.name: discard
splice.desc: Discard all uncommitted changes (asks first)

splice.name: undo
splice.desc: Undo the last commit, amend, merge, rebase, reset, switch or discard (asks first)

splice.name: reflog
splice.desc: Where HEAD has been: see, reset to or check out any earlier position

splice.name: pop
splice.desc: Apply a stash and drop it

splice.name: tag
splice.desc: Create a tag

splice.name: tag-push
splice.desc: Push a tag (to origin unless a remote is named)

splice.name: release
splice.desc: Create a GitHub or GitLab release for a tag, with notes written for you (or from a file)

splice.name: worktree
splice.desc: Add a worktree at a path (relative to the repository), checking out a ref

splice.name: reset
splice.desc: Move the current branch to a ref (soft, mixed or hard)

splice.name: pr
splice.desc: Open a pull request from the current branch

splice.name: comment
splice.desc: Comment on the pull request picked in PRs

splice.name: reply
splice.desc: Reply to a review comment in a pull request's diff (r on it)

splice.name: review-comment
splice.desc: Comment on the line under the cursor in a pull request's diff (c on it)

splice.name: resolve
splice.desc: Mark the review comment picked in a pull request's diff resolved (x on it)

splice.name: unresolve
splice.desc: Open the review comment picked in a pull request's diff again (x on it)

splice.name: merge-pr
splice.desc: Merge the pull request picked in PRs (asks how; --auto once checks pass)

splice.name: ci
splice.desc: CI checks of the pull request picked in PRs: logs, re-run the failed ones

splice.name: reviewer
splice.desc: Ask people to review the pull request picked in PRs

splice.name: draft
splice.desc: Make the pull request picked in PRs a draft

splice.name: ready
splice.desc: Mark the pull request picked in PRs ready for review

splice.name: title
splice.desc: Rename the pull request picked in PRs

splice.name: body
splice.desc: Edit the picked pull request's description: alone, in a file for your editor

splice.name: approve
splice.desc: Approve the pull request picked in PRs

splice.name: request-changes
splice.desc: Ask for changes to the pull request picked in PRs (asks first; GitHub and GitLab need the text)

splice.name: describe
splice.desc: Claude writes the commit message for the staged changes

splice.name: split
splice.desc: Claude splits your uncommitted changes into logical commits, each reviewed before it is made

splice.name: ship
splice.desc: Push the branch, open its pull request (Claude drafts it) and turn on auto-merge, in one go; once merged, switch to the default branch, pull and delete it

splice.name: unlock-worktree
splice.desc: Unlock a locked worktree (the only locked one, or the one at a path; u in Worktrees)

splice.name: run-at
splice.desc: Check a commit (HEAD if none given) out in a worktree of its own (../<repo>-at-<hash>) and copy the line that runs it in Bosun (w in Graph)

splice.name: review-pr
splice.desc: Check a pull request out in a worktree of its own (../<repo>-pr-<n>) and open it, or bring that one up to date (w in PRs)

splice.name: backport
splice.desc: Cherry-pick a merged pull request onto a release branch, as backport/<n>-to-<branch>, push it and open its pull request (asks first)

splice.name: changelog
splice.desc: Claude writes release notes from the commits and merged PRs since a tag (the latest by default); --into-release: the notes of that release

splice.name: draft-pr
splice.desc: Claude drafts a pull request (title and description) for the current branch

splice.name: explain
splice.desc: Claude explains a commit (HEAD if none given)

splice.name: review
splice.desc: Claude reviews a commit, or your changes if none given

splice.name: reword
splice.desc: New message for the commit picked in the rebase editor

splice.name: bisect
splice.desc: Find the commit that brought in a problem: mark commits good or bad (HEAD if no ref), run a command that tests each (exit 0 good, 125 skip, else bad), reset to stop

splice.name: continue
splice.desc: Continue the merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert

splice.name: abort
splice.desc: Abort the merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert

splice.name: history
splice.desc: A file's commits, following renames (deleted files too)

splice.name: blame
splice.desc: Who last changed each line of a file (from that line, given one)

splice.name: owners
splice.desc: Who owns a path by CODEOWNERS, and which line says so; alone, the owners of your changed files

splice.name: future
splice.desc: The open pull requests whose changes touch a line (none given: the line under the cursor of the blame open, or the last one shown; alt+f in blame)

splice.name: note
splice.desc: The note on the graph's commit under the cursor (HEAD elsewhere): text adds or replaces it (\n for a new line); alone, it goes in the prompt to edit; -d removes it (asks); --undo puts back the last one replaced or removed

splice.name: notes
splice.desc: Push the notes (refs/notes/*) to the remote

splice.name: hooks
splice.desc: The active git hooks (core.hooksPath, husky, .git/hooks) and hook frameworks (lefthook, pre-commit): ↵ shows one, r runs it now

splice.name: env
splice.desc: The project's environment (.fleet/project.json), or switch every app to another; in production the frames turn red and a push to the branch it deploys from asks first

splice.name: family
splice.desc: What this repository offers the other apps (Bosun, Hail, Trawl): ↵ copies the command to paste into one

splice.name: timeline
splice.desc: What the family's apps did (pushes, merges, restarts, writes to a database), newest first: p this repository only or all, ↵ an entry whole

splice.name: wiring
splice.desc: What this repository points at: addresses, hosts, ports and connection strings from appsettings*.json, .env and http-client env files, by file (secrets masked)

splice.name: take
splice.desc: What another app copied for Splice: an exception or a file opens blame at its line, a commit its diff

splice.name: find
splice.desc: Filter the graph by message, author or hash; -S <text> or -G <regex> search all history for code changes

splice.name: filter
splice.desc: Show only the commits, on any branch, by an author, touching a path, or in a date range (alone: clear it)

splice.name: open
splice.desc: Open a repository

splice.name: clone
splice.desc: Clone a repository next to the open one (or into the folder Splice started in), then open it

splice.name: scan
splice.desc: Add a folder to scan for repositories

splice.name: last
splice.desc: Show the full output of the last command

splice.name: settings
splice.desc: Every setting, changed in place: accent colour, updates, folders, recent, history

splice.name: accent
splice.desc: The accent colour, saved and repainted straight away

splice.name: refresh
splice.desc: Reload the repository

splice.name: update
splice.desc: Look for a new version of Splice now and install it

splice.name: help
splice.desc: Keyboard shortcuts

splice.name: quit
splice.desc: Exit Splice

trawl.name: connect
trawl.desc: Connect to a saved connection

trawl.name: add
trawl.desc: Save a connection (SQL Server, az login unless --user)

trawl.name: azure-sql
trawl.desc: Connect to an Azure SQL database: the saved connection to it, else one saved as /add would (Sonar copies these)

trawl.name: import
trawl.desc: Add your DataGrip data sources as connections, in their folders

trawl.name: import-csv
trawl.desc: A CSV file as INSERTs into a table, by its header: into a console tab to read (--run runs it)

trawl.name: forget
trawl.desc: Remove a saved connection (and its saved password)

trawl.name: folder
trawl.desc: Put a connection in a folder (no folder takes it out)

trawl.name: password
trawl.desc: Save a login's password in the OS credential store

trawl.name: firewall
trawl.desc: Let this machine through an Azure SQL server's firewall (a rule added through az)

trawl.name: disconnect
trawl.desc: Close the connection

trawl.name: use
trawl.desc: Switch to another database on the same server

trawl.name: open
trawl.desc: Open a script in Query (reloads when you save it)

trawl.name: console
trawl.desc: Back to the console in Query (after /open)

trawl.name: tab
trawl.desc: The console's tabs: open, switch, rename, close ([ and ] switch, + opens)

trawl.name: new
trawl.desc: Clear the console and start typing

trawl.name: format
trawl.desc: Lay out the statement under the cursor in the console (or the selection)

trawl.name: search
trawl.desc: Find text in the console (then n and N: next, previous)

trawl.name: save
trawl.desc: Write the console to a file

trawl.name: snippet
trawl.desc: Run a saved query; save the console's statement as one; forget one

trawl.name: snippets
trawl.desc: The saved queries for this connection: ↵ run, e edit, x forget

trawl.name: describe
trawl.desc: Columns, types and keys of a table or view

trawl.name: script
trawl.desc: CREATE script of a table, view, procedure or function, into the console

trawl.name: script-all
trawl.desc: Every table, view, routine and trigger in a file of its own (<schema>/Tables/<name>.sql…), for git: only changed files are written

trawl.name: migrations
trawl.desc: Migration scripts against the history table (Flyway, EF Core, DbUp, Prisma, Knex, Drizzle, or Trawl's own): applied, pending, changed; run runs the pending (R)

trawl.name: generate
trawl.desc: Rows of made-up test data as INSERTs, in a console tab of their own (nothing runs)

trawl.name: scaffold
trawl.desc: A C# class, EF Core entity, TypeScript interface or Python dataclass for a table or view, copied

trawl.name: diagram
trawl.desc: A table's foreign keys n levels out both ways (every table without one) as boxes and lines; m: Mermaid erDiagram to copy or save (alt+d in the Explorer)

trawl.name: grep
trawl.desc: Every view, procedure, function and trigger whose definition has the text in it: ↵ its CREATE script, at the match

trawl.name: uses
trawl.desc: What refers to a table, view or routine, and what it refers to (u in the Explorer)

trawl.name: find
trawl.desc: Filter the Explorer by name (empty clears it)

trawl.name: filter
trawl.desc: Show only the result rows with a value containing the text (empty shows all)

trawl.name: cell
trawl.desc: The whole value of the cell under the cursor in Results: JSON and XML laid out, binary as hex (v)

trawl.name: follow
trawl.desc: From the cell under the cursor in Results along its foreign key (F)

trawl.name: pin
trawl.desc: Keep the result set on screen to compare a later run with (p in Results)

trawl.name: compare
trawl.desc: This database's schema against another connection's or environment's: only here, only there, different; s the script that brings that one in line (alone: the pinned result against the one on screen, c in Results)

trawl.name: data
trawl.desc: The result set on screen as a table to look into, or the cell's value when it is JSON text, as a tree to open and query with a path like .items[0].name (w in Results)

trawl.name: copy
trawl.desc: Copy the result set on screen (tab-separated pastes into a spreadsheet)

trawl.name: chart
trawl.desc: The result set on screen as a chart, picked from its columns unless named (b in Results; esc back to the grid)

trawl.name: export
trawl.desc: Save the result set on screen (.xlsx: every result set, a sheet each)

trawl.name: watch
trawl.desc: Run a read again every few seconds, changes picked out, until esc (the console's statement without sql; stop ends it)

trawl.name: more
trawl.desc: Fetch another row limit's worth of the result set the limit cut off (m in Results)

trawl.name: limit
trawl.desc: Rows kept per result set (the query stops there)

trawl.name: writes
trawl.desc: Allow writes on a read-only connection until you disconnect

trawl.name: tx
trawl.desc: Commit each statement as it runs, or only on /commit

trawl.name: commit
trawl.desc: Commit the open transaction

trawl.name: undo-write
trawl.desc: The last writes' copies on this connection: ↵ puts the script that undoes one in the console (nothing runs)

trawl.name: rollback
trawl.desc: Roll back the open transaction

trawl.name: settings
trawl.desc: Trawl's settings: row limit, accent colour, updates (,)

trawl.name: update
trawl.desc: Check for a newer Trawl and install it (or say how to get it)

trawl.name: ask
trawl.desc: Claude writes a query for it, into the console (nothing runs)

trawl.name: ai
trawl.desc: What Claude may see of a connection (schema only by default)

trawl.name: stats
trawl.desc: Pages read per table and server time after each run (STATISTICS IO, TIME)

trawl.name: plan
trawl.desc: The estimated plan of the console's statement (nothing runs); actual runs it, for the rows each step really gave (P)

trawl.name: diff
trawl.desc: Compare this database's schema with another's, and offer the script that makes this one match

trawl.name: health
trawl.desc: A check-up of this database: missing, unused and doubled indexes, keys, constraints, statistics, triggers; then offers the fixes as a script

trawl.name: sizes
trawl.desc: Every table's rows and space (reserved, data, indexes), biggest first, in Results

trawl.name: deadlocks
trawl.desc: The server's recent deadlocks: who waited for whom, each one's SQL and the locks

trawl.name: fanout
trawl.desc: One read-only query on every connection in a folder, the rows merged (the console's statement without sql)

trawl.name: activity
trawl.desc: The server's sessions: what runs, what waits, who blocks whom (6)

trawl.name: jobs
trawl.desc: SQL Agent's jobs: running now, last outcome, next run; ↵ their runs, s starts one (alt+j in Activity)

trawl.name: top-queries
trawl.desc: The queries that cost the most: Query Store, else the plan cache; o sorts (alt+q in Activity)

trawl.name: kill
trawl.desc: End another session (KILL), after asking; read-only connections refuse it

trawl.name: why
trawl.desc: Claude explains the last error and puts a corrected statement in the console (nothing runs)

trawl.name: explain-slow
trawl.desc: A statement slow in production (Sonar's /slow-sql hands one over), or the console's: its estimated plan (never run), then Claude on indexes, its DDL left in a console tab as text

trawl.name: explain
trawl.desc: Claude explains the last plan (p): what it does, what costs most, what might help

trawl.name: api
trawl.desc: Claude writes an HTTP endpoint that runs the console's statement, in the project's language (s saves it); copies a request for Hail

trawl.name: copyrows
trawl.desc: Copy rows (and the rows they refer to) to another connection or environment, personal data masked: a preview says what each column gets; a key already there stops it; production asks first

trawl.name: copy-rows
trawl.desc: Copy rows (and the rows they refer to) to another connection, personal data made up; the script shows first (alt+c in Results and the Explorer)

trawl.name: rehearse
trawl.desc: Run a migration (the console, or a file) inside a transaction that is rolled back: each statement's time, rows and errors, and the locks it held

trawl.name: backup
trawl.desc: Back up the database you're in (not production or read-only): BACKUP … COPY_ONLY to the server's backup folder, or pg_dump / mysqldump here

trawl.name: restore
trawl.desc: Restore a backup into a database, made or replaced (asking first); not on production or read-only connections

trawl.name: export-bacpac
trawl.desc: Export the database you're in as a .bacpac (schema and data) with SqlPackage; Azure SQL Database too; --no-data leaves some tables' data out

trawl.name: import-bacpac
trawl.desc: Import a .bacpac as a new database with SqlPackage; not on production or read-only connections

trawl.name: env
trawl.desc: The project's environment (.fleet/project.json): which one, or choose one for every app; Trawl moves to the connection it names, and a production one asks before any write

trawl.name: project
trawl.desc: The databases this project's appsettings and .env files name that aren't saved yet: ↵ adds one

trawl.name: family
trawl.desc: What this project offers Splice, Bosun and Hail: ↵ copies the command to paste into theirs

trawl.name: timeline
trawl.desc: What the family's apps did that changed something, newest first: p this project or all, ↵ an entry whole

trawl.name: wiring
trawl.desc: What this project points at (appsettings, .env, Hail's env files): addresses, hosts, ports, connection strings, by file, secrets masked

trawl.name: take
trawl.desc: Take what Splice, Sonar, Bosun or Hail copied: a query into a console tab, rows as an INSERT

trawl.name: share
trawl.desc: Copy the console's statement, or the row under the cursor in Results (all: every row), for the family (t)

trawl.name: last
trawl.desc: Show the full output of the last run

trawl.name: refresh
trawl.desc: Reload the schema

trawl.name: help
trawl.desc: Keyboard shortcuts

trawl.name: quit
trawl.desc: Exit Trawl

sonar.name: kql
sonar.desc: Run a query in Logs, against the Application Insights in scope

sonar.name: queries
sonar.desc: Your saved queries (s in Logs saves one): pick one to run, or name it

sonar.name: chart
sonar.desc: Draw the result in Logs as a chart (a time series as sparklines, names as bars), or as the grid again

sonar.name: export
sonar.desc: Save the grid in Logs to a file: .csv, .json or .md (a Markdown table)

sonar.name: sub
sonar.desc: Another subscription (a list to pick from if none is named)

sonar.name: insights
sonar.desc: The Application Insights that Logs and Problems look in, or a Log Analytics workspace for Logs to query

sonar.name: find
sonar.desc: Show only the apps whose name or resource group has the text in it (none: all of them)

sonar.name: appsettings
sonar.desc: An app's or slot's settings, to see, edit or compare

sonar.name: compare
sonar.desc: How a slot's settings differ from another slot's of the same app

sonar.name: restart
sonar.desc: Restart an app or slot (asks first; production asks for its name)

sonar.name: stop
sonar.desc: Stop an app or slot (asks first)

sonar.name: start
sonar.desc: Start a stopped app or slot

sonar.name: swap
sonar.desc: Swap a slot into production (asks for the app's name)

sonar.name: functions
sonar.desc: A function app's functions: trigger, on or off, runs and failures over the span; ↵ runs in Logs, i invokes, d turns off/on

sonar.name: scale
sonar.desc: Scale the App Service plan an app runs on: so many instances, or a tier such as P1v3 (asks first; says which apps share it)

sonar.name: route
sonar.desc: Send a share of an app's production traffic to a slot (testing in production); 0 stops it (asks first)

sonar.name: deployments
sonar.desc: An app's or slot's deployments: who, when, how it went; ↵ shows one's log

sonar.name: domains
sonar.desc: An app's custom domains from the outside: DNS (A, AAAA, CNAME, CAA, MX), redirects from http:// and the bare domain, https enforced or not, the certificate's days left

sonar.name: changes
sonar.desc: What changed an app or slot over the span, the marks on the charts: deployments, swaps, settings saved, restarts, the family's changes; ↵ one whole (who, when, its commit)

sonar.name: locker
sonar.desc: Copy an app or slot for Locker, to compare its settings with this folder's and its key vault

sonar.name: trawl
sonar.desc: Copy a command that opens a SQL database (or server) in Trawl, to paste into Trawl's prompt (checks the firewall first)

sonar.name: firewall
sonar.desc: Let this machine's address through a SQL server's firewall (asks first)

sonar.name: portal
sonar.desc: Open an app or slot (or whatever is under the cursor in Resources) in the Azure portal

sonar.name: why
sonar.desc: Ask Claude why a problem happens, from its latest occurrence (and the code, when Sonar runs in the app's folder)

sonar.name: incident
sonar.desc: A problem as an incident: when, how often, the deployments before it, its latest occurrence, failing SQL, commits to its files; save writes the write-up

sonar.name: slow-sql
sonar.desc: The app's slowest SQL over the span (95th percentile), from Application Insights' dependencies: ↵ copies one for Trawl's /explain-slow, which plans it and asks Claude about indexes

sonar.name: compare-window
sonar.desc: Two equal windows before and after the latest deployment (or a time, or the middle of the span): exceptions new, gone or twice as frequent, dependencies slower, operations failing more

sonar.name: watch
sonar.desc: Pin a query whose first value is a number, run every few minutes against the Application Insights in scope; going over the threshold notifies

sonar.name: watches
sonar.desc: Your watches and what they said last: ↵ runs one in Logs, x removes it

sonar.name: posture
sonar.desc: The subscription's security posture (or one resource group's), read through Resource Graph: storage, NSGs and VMs, apps, SQL, key vaults, Redis, Cosmos DB, registries, Defender's recommendations; worst first, ↵ one with the az command that fixes it

sonar.name: env
sonar.desc: The project's environment (dev, staging, prod… in .fleet/project.json): none says which, a name switches every app; its sonar section picks the app and its Application Insights

sonar.name: take
sonar.desc: What another app copied for Sonar: a commit's deployments, problems like an exception, a log line's request

sonar.name: timeline
sonar.desc: What the family's apps did that changed something (pushes, writes, restarts, swaps…), newest first: p this project only or all, ↵ an entry whole

sonar.name: wiring
sonar.desc: What this folder points at: addresses, hosts, ports and connection strings in appsettings*.json, .env and http-client env files, by file (secrets masked)

sonar.name: family
sonar.desc: What this folder is to the other apps (its checkout, processes, .http files, databases): ↵ copies a line for one's prompt

sonar.name: run
sonar.desc: Run a shell command (as ! does)

sonar.name: last
sonar.desc: All the output of the last command

sonar.name: settings
sonar.desc: Theme, accent colour, mouse, updates, notifications, watches, family moods, history

sonar.name: accent
sonar.desc: Change the accent colour (default puts it back)

sonar.name: update
sonar.desc: Look for a new version of Sonar now and install it

sonar.name: help
sonar.desc: Keys and commands

sonar.name: quit
sonar.desc: Exit Sonar

bosun.name: restart
bosun.desc: Restart a process, a group, or all of them

bosun.name: stop
bosun.desc: Stop a process (or a group) and what it started

bosun.name: build
bosun.desc: Build, then restart (or start) a process, a group, or all of them

bosun.name: start
bosun.desc: Start a process, a group, or all that aren't running

bosun.name: log
bosun.desc: Everything a process has said

bosun.name: save-log
